[128] Strong security policy developments and that NATO's role as a consultation body is strengthened

[129] Norway is therefore actively working to ensure that the alliance retains its security policy relevance for the member states on both sides of the Atlantic

[130] In Norway's view, NATO should be a central consultation body in all matters affecting the security of the member states

[131] At the same time, it is important for Norway to take part in European security and defense cooperation, which, despite challenges, has developed rapidly in recent years

[132] The decision that Norway, together with Sweden, Finland and Estonia, will create a Nordic military task force for the EU is an important step in this regard

[133] Norway will continue its efforts to further develop NATO's and the EU's military capacities in mutual harmony, so that the organizations complement each other through close cooperation

[134] The political development in Russia is important for the development in our neighboring areas – both in the Baltic Sea area and the northern areas

[135] Although developments in the country have shown many positive features, it is individual trends that give cause for concern

[136] It is therefore necessary for Norway to follow the political, economic and military developments in Russia in general, and the northern regions in particular

[137] At the same time, it is important for Norway to contribute to the international effort to engage Russia in close and comprehensive cooperation through the NATO-Russia Council

[257] Security policy developments and main Norwegian priorities For a detailed explanation of the security and defense policy framework conditions, the government refers to St.prp

[258] No. 42 (2003–

[259] The further modernization of the Armed Forces in the period 2005–

[260] P. no. 234 (2003–

[261] The security policy chapter in this proposal summarizes the central points in the security policy statement in St.prp

[262] no. 42 (2003–2004), and updates these according to the developments that have taken place up to autumn 2005. Norway's security policy interests Norway's overall security policy interests are formulated in the overall objectives

[263] The Storting has set Norwegian security policy

[264] These are: – to prevent war and the emergence of various threats to Norwegian and collective security; – to contribute to peace, stability and further development of the international legal order; – to safeguard Norwegian sovereignty, Norwegian rights and interests and protect Norwegian freedom of action against political, military and other pressure; – together with our allies to defend Norway and NATO against attacks and attacks; to secure society against attacks and attacks by state and non-state actors

[265] To effectively safeguard our security policy interests

[266] must Norway be able to use a whole range of security policy instruments, including political, legal, police, diplomatic, economic, informational, humanitarian and military ones

[267] In this context, the defense is a central tool for the Norwegian authorities both in our local areas and internationally, also in situations where the active use of military force is not required

[268] The interaction between intelligence, maritime surveillance aircraft, radar chain, AIS, the regional command on Reitan and the Coast Guard in the northern areas is an example of this

[269] Also regular presence of other navy, air defense and allies as trainers in Norway, constitutes a whole in this

[270] Active use of military force in certain situations represents a last resort when other means cannot be used or have failed

[271] Norwegian security is closely linked to international security

[272] Norway must therefore have a global perspective in its security policy approach

[273] The main pillars of Norwegian security policy are the UN and NATO

[274] Norway attaches decisive importance to the UN as a global and overall security policy anchor, which has the primary responsibility for safeguarding international peace and security

[275] Within the framework set by the UN, NATO forms the main pillar of Norwegian security policy

[276] It is an important goal for Norway, and clearly in our own interest, to contribute to strengthening international security by participating actively and constructively in both the UN and NATO

[277] By actively participating in peace operations under the auspices of these organisations, including stabilization operations, Norway contributes not only to ensuring international peace and security, but also to strengthening multilateral cooperation and the multilateral institutions. 2.2 Security policy challenges

[278] In safeguarding our security policy interests, Norway faces a number of actual and potential challenges both locally and globally

[279] However, today's unpredictable and unmanageable risk picture means that a unilateral focus on conventional defense of Norwegian territory no longer constitutes a sufficient guarantee for our security

[280] In the short and medium term, there is no threat of a conventional military attack against

[281] from another state

[282] Norwegian security is best safeguarded by contributing to peace, security and stability, both globally and in nearby Norwegian areas

[283] It is in Norway's interest to contribute to preventing the development and spread of crises, armed conflicts and wars, including international terrorism, which can directly or indirectly threaten our own security

[284] such a development, Norway must demonstrate the will and ability to take responsibility for its own security and quickly meet any acute security challenges

[285] At the same time, we must create the conditions for political support and, if necessary, military assistance from our allies, should the situation require it

[286] In Norway's neighboring areas, it is especially in the north, where we have abundant natural resources and border the great power Russia, that the goal of stable and predictable development is important

[287] In this connection, monitoring, asserting sovereignty and exercising authority in the extensive sea areas in the north constitute particularly challenging tasks for the Norwegian Armed Forces

[288] Globally, international terrorism and the spread of weapons of mass destruction and means of mass destruction constitute the most serious threats

[289] The terrorist attacks in London and Sharm el-Sheikh in the summer of 2005 gave us another reminder of this

[290] Like a number of other countries, Norway also appears as a possible target for international terrorism

[291] Norway works both locally and globally to meet the threat from international terrorism and the spread of weapons and means of mass destruction

[292] Locally, we do this by continuously working to improve preparedness and security against these threats

[293] Globally, we contribute to the international work for non-proliferation and the fight against international terrorism

[294] The defence's considerable and modernized resources constitute an important resource in this work, both at home and abroad

[295] Important security policy developments Many aspects of the international developments we see today are of great importance to Norway and Norwegian security policy interests

[296] This applies both to the changes underway in the UN and NATO, the development in the relationship between Europe and the USA, the continued strengthening of security and defense policy cooperation in the EU and the political development in Russia and regions such as the Middle East and Asia

[297] It is clearly in Norway's interest to strengthen the UN and NATO's ability to meet the security challenges facing the international community today

[298] Norway therefore actively supports the reform work that is ongoing in both organisations

[299] The UN focuses on strengthening its ability to plan and lead peace operations, including increased use of regional organizations such as NATO, the EU and the AU to carry out operations

[300] NATO has reformed its command structure and ability to lead new parallel operations and is now in a period of reform which, among other things, will include a reorganization of NATO headquarters in Brussels

[301] The work to strengthen NATO's ability to handle changed security challenges and tasks is also important in relation to the maintenance and strengthening of transatlantic cooperation

[302] The operation in Iraq in particular has led to disagreement between key NATO countries

[303] Although the relationship across the Atlantic has by now largely normalized, challenges remain

[304] It is clearly in Norway's interest that the transatlantic ties remain strong and that NATO is strengthened as a security policy consultation body

[305] Also for this reason, Norway chooses to continue its prioritization of operations under the auspices of NATO

[306] It is important that all nations contribute to the operations NATO has collectively decided to engage in

[307] This concerns operations that either have a formal UN mandate or that the UN has called for

[308] The European Union takes aim

[309] to take greater responsibility for security in Europe and globally, in line with the EU's security strategy

[310] Despite the fact that the EU's member states have also had problems in agreeing on individual issues, the EU's security and defense policy cooperation has developed rapidly in recent years

[311] Central to the work to develop the EU's crisis management capability is the decision to create military and civilian task forces

[312] It is important for Norway to take part in European security and defense cooperation, which we do, among other things. through the creation of a Nordic military task force for the EU, together with Sweden, Finland and Estonia

[313] At the same time, it is in Norway's interest to work for NATO's and the EU's military capacities to be complementary, so as to contribute to the organizations complementing each other through close cooperation, rather than competing

[314] The UN, NATO and the EU are all working to meet the security challenges of our time, where terrorism and the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction and their means of delivery, including missile technology, are the most serious

[315] This work takes place on several levels, with a number of security policy tools and in different parts of the world

[316] At the military level, NATO and Norway give special priority to the work to ensure stability and peaceful development in Afghanistan

[317] Another important goal is to contribute to stability and constructive development in the Middle East area

[318] NATO's contribution to enable an Iraqi popularly elected government to take control of its own country, and the EU's negotiations on non-proliferation of nuclear weapons with Iran, are important in this regard

[319] Peace and stability in this part of the world is also in Norway's interest, and one we have long

[320] has sought to achieve in the conflict between Israel and the Palestinians

[321] Developments in parts of the world that have traditionally attracted less security policy attention here in Norway may also gain increasing importance in the years to come

[322] This applies to Africa, where the EU in particular has taken a more active role both directly and indirectly in its support for the African Union, but also Asia

[323] The situation in Asia is characterized by partly strong underlying conflicts of interest and military build-up, which can lead to a serious potential for conflict

[324] Partly as a result of this, the US is increasingly focusing on developments in Asia

[325] North Korea's development of weapons of mass destruction represents a potential threat to world peace which could have extensive, if perhaps only indirect, consequences for Norway as well

[326] China's growing economic and military strength will probably change the security policy balance in Asia in the coming years

[327] This will impose a special responsibility on China to contribute to a stable and peaceful development in both Asia and the Pacific region, which benefits the entire world community

[328] In more domestic areas, the political development of Russia, our superpower neighbour, is important for the development of our neighboring areas – both in the Baltic Sea region and the northern regions

[329] Although the development in Russia has shown many positive features, it is individual trends that give cause for concern

[330] It is therefore necessary for Norway to follow the political, economic and military developments in Russia in general, and the northern regions in particular

[331] At the same time, it is important for Norway to contribute to the international work to engage Russia in close and comprehensive cooperation through the NATO-Russia Council. Participation in military operations abroad The armed forces' participation in military operations abroad is an integral and important part of Norwegian security and defense policy

[332] Our participation abroad strengthens international and thus also Norwegian security

[333] Through our commitment, we contribute to peace and demonstrate solidarity with the international community, and we fulfill the political obligations we have undertaken as a result of membership in international organizations such as NATO and the UN

[334] Our involvement also contributes to maintaining close contact and good cooperation with allied countries, and to Norwegian forces gaining useful operational experience

[335] Moreover, this type of activity is an important element in the fight against global terrorism, in order to contribute to peace and to a positive political and economic development in other parts of the world

[336] It is a prerequisite for Norwegian participation in foreign operations that they are anchored in international law in the form of a UN mandate or other recognized basis of international law

[337] Furthermore, emphasis is placed on the fact that it is a suitable multinational framework around our contributions, in the form of the UN, NATO, the EU or possibly a multinational coalition

[338] In 2006, we broadly aim to continue our involvement at the same level as in

[339] The international military presence in Afghanistan takes place within the framework of the NATO-led operation ISAF, and the US-led coalition OEF (Operation Enduring Freedom

[340] The main focus area for Norway in 2006 will be ISAF (International Security Assistance Force), where we will participate with approximately 380 people

[341] The main challenge for NATO will be further ISAF expansion beyond the provinces

[342] Today, ISAF operates in the north and west of the country

[343] already in

[344] one begins the expansion southwards, and gradually eastwards

[345] Here, the security situation is more difficult, and there is thus a need for more robust military forces, including flexible emergency forces and air support

[654] The framework conditions of the defense are changing

[655] An unpredictable security picture, rapid technological development and changes in international cooperation patterns create significant challenges, and mean that the government attaches great importance to having a holistic approach to the alignment and further development of the Armed Forces

[656] For the period 2005–2008, the following defense policy goals govern the activities of the Armed Forces: – Alone and together with allies secure Norwegian sovereignty, Norwegian rights and interests, and preserve Norwegian freedom of action against military and other pressure – together with allies, through participation in multinational peace operations and international defense cooperation to contribute to peace, stability, enforcement of international law and respect for human rights and prevent the use of force by states and non-state actors against Norway and NATO – together with allies, contribute to the collective defense of Norway and other allies in accordance with our alliance obligations, and to meet various types of attacks and attacks with coercive power to ensure Norwegian and collective security - help to safeguard Norwegian social security, save lives and limit the consequences of accidents, disasters, attacks and attacks from state and non-state actors

[1482] no. 1 48 Ministry of Defense Box 3.1 New combat aircraft The Air Force's F-16 fighter has recently been upgraded, and is today a very modern combat aircraft

[1483] The aircraft's limitation lies in the fact that each airframe has a finite lifespan, which means that within a few years a decision must be made regarding the acquisition of a new combat aircraft to replace the F

[1484] In this connection, it is important to emphasize that a modern and high-quality fighter aircraft forms an essential part of the inventory of a modern defence

[1485] This does not just apply if the country is exposed to a direct attack, but also in connection with the assertion of sovereignty and crisis management

[1486] In a modern conflict, air superiority will usually be the factor that contributes more than anything else to deciding the outcome of the battles, also on the hill or at sea

[1487] The importance of air superiority has been very clearly demonstrated in a number of wars and conflicts since the Second World War

[1488] Only when air supremacy has been established have other operations been launched, and then the decision has come very quickly, regardless of the balance of forces on the hill

[1489] A Norwegian defense without a fighter air force which, together with allied aircraft, can contribute to ensuring air superiority over its own areas will be in such a great imbalance that this greatly reduces the value of other materiel acquisitions

[1490] Furthermore, without combat aircraft, Norway will not be able to assert its national sovereignty or conduct independent crisis management in Norwegian airspace and adjacent international airspace

[1491] The airspace is a part of the territory that is highly exposed in terms of challenges to a state's sovereignty and attempts to put it under political pressure in connection with crises

[1492] This is because the violation of airspace by warplanes is a very clear signal of political and military intention and strength, while at the same time the great speed and range of the planes means that the situation can be quickly normalized after such an overflight if desired

[1493] Air power is therefore a decisive and flexible tool for graded demonstration of military power for political purposes

[1494] The ability to assert sovereignty in its own airspace and to be able to oppose such violations thus becomes equally important for a state that wants to preserve its political freedom of action and secure an ability to resist political pressure. The main direction for the development of the Armed Forces is based on a future defense that is modern, flexible and taskbased

[1495] The combat aircraft's characteristics support the strong prioritization that is placed on the ability to quickly solve the entire spectrum of the Defence's priority tasks, both at home and abroad

[1496] Norway must have the right to dispose of a set of effective military capacities that ensure the necessary national room for action in a crisis situation

[1497] At the same time, we must be able to provide the required capacities for the communities we are part of

[1498] The combat aircraft as a platform has characteristics that make it hardly relevant in any defense structure in the foreseeable future, and will contribute to giving Norway a credible defense capable of solving the tasks assigned at any time

[1499] Possibly a renewal of the fighter fleet will constitute a very significant investment for the Armed Forces, also financially

[2466] Personnel, education and competence

[2467] The reorganization will continue to place great demands on the personnel

[2468] A new command system has been implemented to ensure that the Army has the right skills and an appropriate age and rank structure

[2469] It is a goal that the structure of the personnel corps balances the Army's needs over time

[2470] In particular, the department commander scheme will strengthen the level of experience and competence at lower levels in the organisation

[2471] The introduction of department commanders started in 2005 and will be expanded further in

[2472] In addition, the development of the Army's departments in a tangible and deployable direction will lead to an increased number of enlisted men

[2473] The Army has implemented a new command school model, where basic command training is sought to be carried out in the operational departments of the Army's forces, as well as at the Army's command school

[2474] These changes will form the basis for the capacity increase that is planned in the long term, especially with regard to the recruitment of enlisted men and department commanders

[2475] Recruitment of personnel across the entire structural spectrum must be ensured, not least for departments on high readiness which must be able to be deployed for multinational operations, where the basis for recruitment and training is mainly arranged in accordance with departmental education in Northern Norway

[2476] The focus on the personnel side in 2006 will therefore be the recruitment and competence development of personnel for the Army's rapid reaction force, the Army's fighter command and other departments that must be able to participate in multinational operations

[2477] In 2006, the Army will educate and train approximately the same number of conscripts as in

[2480] The focus will be on the Army's primary activities and the departments' operational capability

[2481] The need for special/subject expertise will be greater in the new structure and will be given special attention

[2513] The navy must consist of flexible and mobile forces with a short reaction time

Organization and force structure The restructuring of the Norwegian Navy's organization continues and gives the defense branch an organization that strengthens operational capability and provides increased availability

[2516] The Navy is organized along three pillars: the Coast Guard, and the Navy's schools

[2517] Minor adjustments have been made to the distribution of tasks between the pillars

[2518] The Coast Guard is led by a staff in Oslo with KV Sør located at Haakonsvern and KV North at Sortland

[2519] In the Coast Guard, structural changes are being made which overall strengthen the Navy's operational units and facilitate better coordination of training, education and force production

[2520] The flotilla division is replaced by a division with weapons for each of the various vessels and units

[2521] Each weapon gets its own training environment so that a larger part of the Navy's employees are transferred to the force-producing link

[2522] At the same time, the operational logistical support, which was previously organized in the flotillas, is brought together in an organizational unit which supports all the navy's vessels. The Marine Hunter Command, the Coastal Hunter Command and the Mine Diver Command are continued. The navy's schools are still organized into KNM Tordenskjold, KNM Harald Haarfagre, the Naval Academy and the Officers' School, but will have changed tasks and reduced staffing

[2523] The basic education as per currently carried out at KNM Tordenskjold, will be partly transferred to the training environments

[2524] The naval officer's school will continue and, according to the plans, will carry out joint admissions with the other officer's schools from

[2528] These changes and assessments will form the basis for later in the long-term period to increase the capacity again, especially with regard to the recruitment of enlisted men and department commanders

[2529] In the coming years, competence development for, and manning of, new frigates and MTBs will constitute a main challenge for the Norwegian Navy

[2530] Officer training is sought to be made more efficient and adapted to future needs and the adjustments in the officer system

[2531] In particular, the department commander scheme will strengthen the level of experience and continuity at lower levels in the organisation

[2532] The department commander scheme will be able to be used in a wide range of positions with requirements for technical competence

[2533] Introduction of department commanders will have to happen gradually, after resources are freed up and competent personnel

[2534] are trained, and the ramp-up will continue in

[2535] The activities at the Navy's schools will be modernized and directed towards a new structure

[2536] The need for special/subject expertise will be greater in the new structure, and special attention will therefore be given

[2648] Overall tasks The changes in the risk picture mean that HV's traditional tasks will no longer be the sole determinant of HV's structure

[2649] After the quality reform has been carried out, a modernized HV will be relevant for sovereignty assertion and national crisis management missions, and for assistance in safeguarding social security in general

[2650] HV must be able to reinforce other military presence in exposed areas and take care of other types of special missions such as reinforced border guarding, force protection, security of national forces and reception of allied reinforcements

[2651] In addition, HV can provide assistance to civil authorities upon request

[2652] HV must therefore be put in a better position to be able to solve more extensive territorial and force protection tasks, and concentrate forces where the need arises

[2653] For these purposes, HV is in the process of developing a core of forces on high alert - task forces - while the more traditional tasks are handled locally by reinforcement and follow-up forces

[2654] The Home Guard District Commanders are territorial commanders in peace, crisis and war, subordinate to the Commander of the Joint Operational Headquarters

[2655] Organization and force structure HV's new district structure with 13 districts was established on 1 August

[2656] HV's new force structure with intervention, reinforcement and follow-up forces of 5,000, 20,000 and 25,000 personnel respectively will be established in 2006 in accordance with Instruction

[2657] S. no. 234 (2003–2004), cf. St.prp

[2658] No. 42 (2003–

[2659] In addition, HV must have a reserve of 33,000 personnel

[2660] In total, HV will thereby have a nominal mobilization force of 83,000 personnel

[2661] Personnel The restructuring of HV will continue to place great demands on the personnel

[2662] The staffing structure HV needs in the future must be balanced between commanders and civilians, with the right age composition, something that e.g., achieved through the introduction of a new command system

[2663] The aim is that the structure of the personnel corps balances HV's needs over time

[2664] The implementation of the quality reform also ensures good and correct recruitment from all the defense branches

[2665] Education and training in 2006 will be carried out in accordance with the quality reform in HV

[2666] In 2006, the new training pattern for annual training of home security teams based on operational requirements and priorities will be implemented

[2667] The training is carried out according to a differentiated training pattern, with priority given to commanders, specialists and priority departments

[2668] This means for the task forces, six to 30 days of annual training, and for the reinforcement and follow-up forces up to nine days of annual training for commanders and six days for the crew forces

[2669] Annual training and education will be carried out so that the resources are utilized as best as possible and so that HV's total military capacity is the greatest possible

[2671] of a minimum of four months, and will be continued in 2006 at Værnes for the Landheimevernet

[2672] It is planned to start HV's manning training at Porsangmoen, with a conscript force of approximately the size of a company in January

[2673] Operational forces for the Maritime Security Forces are transferred from the Navy, while personnel for the Luftheimevernet are primarily transferred from the Air Force

[2674] The basic commander's training will be maintained at Værnes and Porsangmoen in 2006, and is adapted to the changes made in basic commander's training in the Armed Forces in general

[2675] HV's own officer training will continue as before through a series of short, targeted courses at Heimevernet’s school and competence center (HVSKS), and will complement the scheme with the transfer of conscripted officers from the defense branches

[2687] In accordance with Act of 20 March 1998 no. 11 on the Intelligence Service, the intelligence service must obtain, process and analyze information that concerns Norwegian interests in relation to foreign states, organizations or individuals

[2688] Against this background, risk analyzes and intelligence assessments must be prepared which can contribute to safeguarding national security interests

[2689] The intelligence service must serve military users and support international missions in which Norway is involved

[2690] This is an ordinary part of the E-service's activity, which must be prioritized and mainly covered within the E-service's budget

[2691] In addition, the service must keep the Ministry of Defense and other affected departments informed of relevant changes in the military and political situation in the Norwegian area of ​​interest

[2692] Contribution to the fight against international terrorism and the spread of weapons of mass destruction constitutes a central and growing part of the E-service's activities

[2693] In areas that serve national interests, cooperation and good relations with similar services in other countries must be established and maintained

[2694] In order to take care of the tasks assigned to the service, emphasis is placed on high professional competence adapted to the new threat picture, and further development of the technical standard

[2695] This, combined with a very rapid and extensive technological development, makes it necessary to implement and continue measures to modernize the service, as well as to make a further shift of resources from less prioritized to prioritized tasks linked to the defense of the future

[3175] UAV – unmanned aerial vehicles (Unmanned Aerial Vehicle). The Swedish Defense Force is considering acquiring a tactical UAV capacity which must be operational from

[3176] The unit consists of a number of UAVs with sensors, and a number of mobile ground stations connected to the information infrastructure

[3177] The UAV capacity is planned to be integrated into the Norwegian Armed Forces' ISTAR unit, but will also be able to be used outside the scope of ISTAR

[3178] A minimum capacity is planned, with the possibility of later capacity expansion

[3179] UAVs are mainly used in situations where manned platforms are not appropriate due to resource use, endurance or risk of loss of human life, and in special situations, such as in areas contaminated by nuclear, radiological, biological or chemical sources

[3180] UAVs will provide the ability to monitor and gather information in near real time, with consequent reduced risk and increased situational awareness, especially in the above situations

[3181] Besides its direct contribution to operations, a tactical UAV capacity will provide valuable expertise that can be used for any later expansion of the capacity area

[3182] Almost all research and development (R&D) in the Armed Forces is financed through the material investment chapter

[3390] Overall objectives Participation in multinational military operations is a central element of our defense and security policy, and serves several key objectives

[3391] First, it demonstrates our country's willingness to take responsibility for ensuring stability and human rights in conflict-affected areas

[3392] Furthermore, it serves our own security by preventing conflicts from spreading and possibly develops into threats against Norway, and contributes to us maintaining good cooperation with key NATO allies, who in turn are guarantors of our own country's security

[3393] Finally, such participation involves ongoing testing and development of the Armed Forces' operational capability

[3574] Arrangements in connection with the first service

[3575] It is assumed that the service time reductions will not have consequences for preparedness or weaken the recruitment basis for multinational peace operations

[3576] Any educational weaknesses must be taken into account to the greatest extent possible when mobilizing the crews, e.g. by transferring them to Heimevernet

[3577] The unemployed have priority when called up for first-time service

[3578] Personnel with sole care for a child are granted a deferral with the first service as long as this status persists and until the end of the year the conscript turns

[3579] Under separate conditions, personnel who run independent livestock farms are granted a deferral of initial service as long as this status persists and until the end of the year in which the conscript turns

[3580] Common provisions For auxiliary service in connection with repetition service and etterutdanningskurs, it can be called inn vernepliktige, who is not mobilized to a military department or at the joint institutions of the Armed Forces

[3581] Conscript personnel (commanders and privates) who are mobilized by staffs or departments, and who are required to train or practice every year, can be called in for a short refresher service/course every year

[3582] Conscripted and discharged

[3583] commanders can be summoned to a refresher course of up to twelve days' duration

[3584] The army can call in conscripted and discharged commanders who say they are willing to command positions and pre-determined key positions at lower and middle level, for a further training course of up to five weeks' duration

[3585] Invitations for a repetition service/course must be made within the framework of the total number of days and number of times set for such service. Doctors, dentists, veterinarians, pharmacists, psychologists, theologians and students in these professions who have completed twelve months' initial service and who have been discharged to (rolled at

[3586] sanitetsstaben or the Field Chaplain Corps, can be called up for 90 days of service at staff or department

[3587] Players can instead serve with forces abroad where Norway participates

[3588] Theologians who have completed 15 months of initial service can be ordered to repeat service three times. Conscript personnel who are given a postponement of their service can be called up to serve residual service at other departments, regardless of the unit leading the roll and, if necessary, in another budget

[3589] In addition to the repetition service, conscripted and discharged commanders, rank and file specialists and special professional groups can be given up to ten days' service for a smaller part of the individual department's organizational plan in war

[3590] Commanders and specialists in the Heimevernet can be given up to three days' service
